q.q: What is a variable?
o: A named value that is set once and cannot change while the program runs
A named memory location whose value can change while the program runs
A value typed in by the user at the keyboard
A named block of code that carries out one task
q.why: A variable is a named store in RAM whose contents can change. The second option is a constant.

q.q: What is a constant?
o: A named value that is set once and stays the same for the whole run of the program
A named memory location whose value can change as the program runs
A value that is calculated from other variables in the program
A variable that is given a starting value of 0 before it is used
q.why: A constant cannot change while the program runs; any line that tries to change it stops the program compiling.

q.q: Which of these should be stored as a constant in a cinema booking program?
o: The customer's name
A running total of takings
The number of seats a customer books
The price of a standard ticket
q.why: The ticket price is fixed while the program runs; the others change with every booking.

q.q: Which is the best identifier for a variable holding the number of pupils on a trip?
o: numPupils
n
Number of pupils
2pupils
q.why: numPupils is meaningful and legal. Identifiers cannot contain spaces or start with a digit, and n is not meaningful.

q.q: A programmer stores the VAT rate as a constant. Which is an advantage?
o: If the rate changes, it only needs updating in one place
It uses less memory than a variable would
It makes the program run faster
The user can change it while the program runs
q.why: One edit updates every calculation that uses the constant. 'It stays the same' alone earns nothing.

q.q: Which is the correct C# declaration of a constant for a pay rate of 11.55 stored as a float?
o: const float RATE_OF_PAY = 11.55;
float const RATE_OF_PAY = 11.55f;
const float RATE_OF_PAY = 11.55f;
const RATE_OF_PAY = 11.55f;
q.why: const comes first and is lower case in C#, a constant needs a data type, and a float literal needs an f.
tickets becomes 5, and total is recalculated as 5 × 7.5 = 37.5. 15 was the value before tickets changed.

q.q: In C#, Total and total are used in the same program. What does this mean?
o: They are two different variables, because C# is case-sensitive
They are the same variable, because C# ignores case
The program will not compile, as identifiers must be in lower case
Total is a constant and total is a variable
q.why: C# is case-sensitive, so Total and total are different identifiers.

q.q: Why is a bare value such as 0.2 in a calculation called a 'magic number'?
o: It is calculated automatically by the compiler when the program runs
It can be changed by the user while the program is running
Its meaning is not explained in the code, whereas a constant such as VAT_RATE explains itself
It is stored in hexadecimal, so it is hard for people to read
q.why: Named constants improve readability; a bare 0.2 does not say what it is.

q.q: What is 23 MOD 5?
q.why: 5 goes into 23 four times (20) with 3 left over; MOD gives the remainder. 4 is 23 DIV 5.

q.q: What is 23 DIV 5?
q.why: DIV gives the whole number of times 5 goes into 23 and throws the remainder away.

q.q: In C#, what is 9 / 2 when both values are int?
q.why: Dividing two ints performs integer division, so the remainder is discarded. 1 is 9 % 2.

q.q: Which C# operator gives the remainder of a division?
o: MOD()
Math.Pow
q.why: In C#, % is MOD. / with two ints is DIV; Math.Pow gives powers.

q.q: What does Math.Pow(2, 3) return?
q.why: Math.Pow(x, y) is x to the power y: 2³ = 8.

q.q: What is the value of 2 + 3 * 4?
q.why: Multiply before adding: 3 × 4 = 12, then 2 + 12 = 14.

q.q: 75 pupils are going on a trip and each minibus seats 16. Which pair of calculations works out how many full minibuses there are and how many pupils are left over?
o: 75 MOD 16 = 4 full minibuses and 75 DIV 16 = 11 left over
75 DIV 16 = 4 full minibuses and 75 MOD 16 = 11 left over
75 / 16 = 4.6875 full minibuses and 75 − 16 = 59 left over
75 DIV 16 = 5 full minibuses and 75 MOD 16 = 5 left over
q.why: DIV gives the full groups and MOD gives the remainder: 4 × 16 = 64, leaving 11 (so 5 minibuses are needed).

q.q: Which test is the standard way to check whether n is an even number?
o: n DIV 2 = 0
n MOD 2 = 0
n MOD 2 = 1
q.why: An even number has no remainder when divided by 2. n MOD 2 = 1 tests for odd.

q.q: Which condition is True only when temp is between 5 and 25 inclusive?
o: temp > 5 && temp < 25
temp >= 5 || temp <= 25
temp >= 5 && temp <= 25
temp == 5 && temp == 25
q.why: Both limits must hold (AND), and inclusive limits need >= and <=. The OR version is true for every number.

q.q: A pupil writes if (score = 10) in C#. What is wrong?
o: = compares values; == is needed to assign a value
The condition needs the word THEN after the brackets
= assigns a value; == is needed to compare two values
Nothing is wrong; = and == mean the same in C#
q.why: In C#, = assigns and == compares, so if (score = 10) is a syntax error.

q.q: Which statement is an assignment?
o: total ← price * quantity
IF total > 10 THEN
OUTPUT total
INPUT total
q.why: Assignment stores the result of the right-hand side in a variable.

q.q: What type of value does Console.ReadLine() return?
o: int
string
double
bool
q.why: It always returns text, which you convert if you need a number.

q.q: count is 4. After count = count + 1 runs, what does count hold?
o: count + 1
q.why: The right side (4 + 1) is worked out first, then stored back in count.

q.q: In which direction is an assignment statement read?
o: Left to right: the variable on the left is worked out, then stored in the expression on the right
Right to left: the expression on the right is worked out, then stored in the variable on the left
Top to bottom: the line above is worked out, then stored in the line below
Either direction, as both sides of = must be equal
q.why: The ← arrow in pseudocode shows the value moving into the variable on the left.

q.q: What is the difference between Console.Write and Console.WriteLine?
o: Write outputs text only; WriteLine outputs numbers only
Write waits for input; WriteLine displays output
Write saves the output to a file; WriteLine shows it on screen
Write leaves the cursor on the same line; WriteLine moves to a new line afterwards
q.why: Console.Write is handy for prompts because the user types on the same line.

q.q: Joining text and values together in an output, as in name + " walked ", is called what?
o: Assignment
Iteration
Concatenation
Conversion
q.why: Concatenation joins strings; C# converts a number to text when it is joined to a string.

q.q: Which statement does the same job as int n = Convert.ToInt32(Console.ReadLine());?
o: int n = Console.ReadLine().ToInt();
int n = (string)Console.ReadLine();
int n = Console.ReadLine(int);
int n = int.Parse(Console.ReadLine());
q.why: int.Parse does the same job and is used in the textbook.

q.q: What does Console.WriteLine("Area: {0:F2} cm²", area); do when area is 12.345?
o: Shows Area: {0:F2} cm² exactly as written
Shows Area: 12.35 cm², replacing {0} with area to 2 decimal places
Shows Area: 0 cm², because {0} means the value zero
Shows Area: 12.345 cm², because F2 only applies to whole numbers
q.why: {0} is replaced by the first value after the text, and :F2 formats it to 2 decimal places.

q.q: What is an array?
o: A data structure that holds values of any mix of data types under one identifier
A data structure that holds many values of the same data type under one identifier
A single named memory location that holds one value
A list of the variable names used in a program and their data types
q.why: An array stores a collection of values of one data type under one name.

q.q:
string[] towns = { "Newry", "Larne", "Strabane" };
What is towns[1]?
o: Larne
Newry
Strabane
An error
q.why: Arrays are zero-indexed, so index 1 is the second element.

q.q: An array has 30 elements. What is the index of the last one?
q.why: Indexes run from 0 to Length − 1.

q.q: Which loop visits every element of a 10-element array called scores?
o: for (int i = 1; i <= 9; i++)
for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++)
for (int i = 1; i < 10; i++)
for (int i = 0; i <= 10; i++)
q.why: Indexes are 0 to 9. Starting at 1 skips the first element, and <= 10 goes out of range.

o: 30 and 5
26 and 5
26 and 4
25 and 5
q.why: votes[2] was 25 and is updated to 26; there are still 5 elements.

q.q:
int[] cars = { 120, 95, 143, 101, 88, 60, 72 };
A loop adds 1 to busyDays for each element greater than 100. What is busyDays after the loop?
q.why: 120, 143 and 101 are greater than 100. 95 and 88 are not.
tallest goes 151, 163, then 170; 159 is not bigger, so 170 remains.

q.q: When finding the smallest value in an array, why should the 'best so far' start as the first element rather than 0?
o: Starting at 0 would make the loop skip the first element
Starting at 0 would cause an index out of range error
Starting at 0 would fail, because 0 may be smaller than every value in the array
Starting at 0 would sort the array into the wrong order
q.why: If best so far began at 0, no positive value would ever replace it as the minimum.

q.q: A loop is written for (int i = 0; i <= cars.Length; i++) to read every element of cars, which has 7 elements. What happens?
o: The last element is skipped, so the total is too small
The first element is skipped, because i starts at 0
The loop never ends, because i can never reach cars.Length
The last pass tries to read cars[7], which does not exist, so the program crashes
q.why: <= Length goes one past the last index; the condition should be i < cars.Length.

q.q: Why would a programmer use a FOR loop instead of a foreach loop to update the elements of an array?
o: foreach can only be used with arrays of strings
foreach visits the elements in reverse order
foreach cannot change the elements or tell you the index
foreach runs one fewer time than the number of elements
q.why: foreach is neat for reading or outputting, but use FOR for updates, searches and sorts.

q.q: In the C# bubble sort, why does the inner loop run to scores.Length - 1 - i?
o: The last i items are already in their final places, and j + 1 must stay inside the array
It makes the sort put the items into descending order
It makes the sort stable, so equal items keep their order
Arrays in C# start at index 1, so one is subtracted
q.why: After pass i the largest i values are at the end, and stopping at Length − 1 keeps j + 1 a valid index.

q.q: What is temp used for in a bubble sort?
o: Counting the number of passes made so far
Storing the largest value found in the pass
Holding one value while two elements are exchanged
Marking whether the list is already sorted
q.why: Without a temporary copy, the first line of the exchange would overwrite one of the values.

q.q:
int[] scores = { 31, 8, 25, 14, 6 };
After the first pass of an ascending bubble sort, what is the array?
q.why: 31 is swapped with each neighbour in turn and bubbles to the end. The last option is the result after pass 2.

q.q: Which three lines correctly exchange list[j] and list[j + 1]?
o: list[j] = list[j + 1]; list[j + 1] = list[j]; temp = list[j];
temp = list[j]; list[j + 1] = temp; list[j] = list[j + 1];
list[j + 1] = temp; temp = list[j]; list[j] = list[j + 1];
temp = list[j]; list[j] = list[j + 1]; list[j + 1] = temp;
q.why: Save list[j] in temp, copy list[j + 1] over it, then put temp into list[j + 1]. The wrong orders leave a duplicate and lose a value.

q.q: In a modified bubble sort, what is the swapped flag for?
o: It counts the number of swaps so the total can be output at the end
It stores the value being moved while two items are exchanged
It records whether any swap happened in a pass, so the sort stops after a pass with none
It records which pass the sort is on, up to n − 1 passes
q.why: A Boolean swapped flag lets the loop end as soon as a pass makes no exchanges.

q.q: In the insertion sort code, why is items[i] copied into current first?
o: So the number of comparisons can be counted
Because C# arrays cannot be read twice
So it is not lost when larger items are shifted right over its position
So the array is sorted into descending order
q.why: Shifting overwrites items[i]; current keeps the value until the gap is found.

q.q: In the C# insertion sort, the WHILE condition is j >= 0 && items[j] > current. Why is j >= 0 checked first?
o: Checking j first makes the sort stable, so equal items keep their order
C# always evaluates the right-hand side of && first, so the order does not matter
C# stops evaluating && when one side is False, so items[j] is never read with j = -1
It makes sure that j is always an even number when the array is read
q.why: Short-circuit evaluation stops an out-of-range read of items[-1].

q.q: Why does a BubbleSort(int[] list) method need no return value?
o: C# methods are not allowed to return arrays
The sorted array is printed inside the method, so it does not need to be kept
A void method automatically returns the last array it changed
The array is passed as a reference to the same data, so the caller's array is sorted directly
q.why: Arrays are passed by reference, so the method sorts the original array.

q.q: In which loop does the insertion sort start, and why?
o: A FOR loop from index 0, because every item must be inserted including the first
A WHILE loop from the last index, because items are inserted from the end
A FOR loop from index 1, because the first item on its own is already a sorted list
A FOR loop from index 1, because index 0 is never used in C# arrays
q.why: The outer loop starts at 1 because the item at index 0 counts as sorted.

q.q: In the linear search, what does the condition pos < tickets.Length && found == false do?
o: Sorts the array before the search begins
Makes the search faster than a binary search
Checks that the array is in order
Keeps the loop going while there are items left and the target has not been found
q.why: The loop needs both items left to check AND the target still not found.

q.q: A linear search function returns −1. What does this mean?
o: The target is the last element
The array is empty
The target is at index 1
The target was not found
q.why: −1 can never be a real index, so it is used to signal 'not found'.

q.q:
int[] tickets = { 412, 87, 903, 255, 61, 730 };
What does LinearSearch(tickets, 255) return, where the function returns the index of the target?
q.why: 255 is the fourth element, at index 3. 4 would be the position counted from 1.

q.q: A linear search finds the target at index 3. What should be output to tell a user it is the fourth item?
o: pos - 1
pos
pos + 1
tickets[pos]
q.why: Index 3 is the fourth item, so output pos + 1. tickets[pos] is the value, not the position.

q.q: In the C# binary search, items[mid] is less than the target. What happens next?
o: first = mid + 1
last = mid - 1
found = true
mid = mid + 1
q.why: The target must be in the upper half, so the lower half including mid is discarded by moving first.

q.q:
int[] items = { 4, 9, 15, 22, 30, 37, 41, 58, 63, 70, 88 };
A binary search with mid = first + (last - first) / 2 looks for 63. Which positions are checked?
o: Position 5 (37), then position 7 (58), then position 8 (63)
Position 6 (41), then position 8 (63)
Position 5 (37), then position 8 (63)
Position 0 (4) to position 8 (63) in turn
q.why: first = 0, last = 10, so mid = 5 (37). 37 < 63, so first = 6 and mid = 6 + 2 = 8, which holds 63.

q.q:
int[] items = { 4, 9, 15, 22, 30, 37, 41, 58, 63, 70, 88 };
A binary search looks for 15. How many comparisons does it make?
q.why: mid = 5 (37) is too big, so last = 4; mid = 2 holds 15: two comparisons.

q.q: Why does a binary search use integer division in mid = first + (last - first) / 2?
o: It makes sure mid is always an even number
It rounds mid up so the upper half is always checked first
It stops the loop when the target is found
It throws away any half, so mid is always a whole index
q.why: Integer division discards any fraction, giving a valid index.

q.q: A binary search loop has no found test and does not change first or last after a match. What could happen?
o: The search would skip the first element
The array would be sorted into the wrong order
The program would not compile
The loop could run for ever
q.why: Without a way to stop after a match, the loop condition never becomes false.

q.q: What does "Derry".Length return?
q.why: D-e-r-r-y is five characters.

q.q: What is "Antrim".Substring(2, 2)?
o: ntr
nt
tr
tri
q.why: Start at index 2 ('t') and take 2 characters. The second number is a length, not an end position.

q.q: With town = "Enniskillen", what is town.Substring(5)?
o: skillen
Ennis
killen
illen
q.why: Substring with one number takes everything from that index to the end; index 5 is 'k'.

q.q: What is "Belfast".IndexOf('f')?
o: True
q.why: B is 0, e 1, l 2, f 3. IndexOf returns a position; Contains returns True or False.

q.q: What does "Newry".IndexOf('z') return?
o: False
q.why: IndexOf returns −1 when the character is not in the string.

q.q: What does "a,b,c".Split(',') return?
o: An array of three strings: "a", "b" and "c"
The number 3, counting the parts
An array with one string, "a,b,c"
The single string "abc" with the commas removed
q.why: Split breaks the string at each separator into an array.

o: Murphy
q.why: parts[0] is Murphy, parts[1] is 11B and parts[2] is 87.

o: AoifeTaylor22
A Taylor 22
ATaylor22
ATaylor
q.why: first[0] is 'A', joined to "Taylor" and then 22.

q.q: town = "Omagh"; A program runs town.ToUpper(); and then outputs town. What is output, and why?
o: OMAGH, because ToUpper changes the original string
omagh, because ToUpper switches the case of every letter
Omagh, because strings are immutable and the new string returned was not stored
An error, because ToUpper must be given a parameter
q.why: ToUpper returns a new string; you must write town = town.ToUpper(); to keep it.

q.q: Which C# condition is a suitable format check that an email address contains an @ sign?
o: email.Length >= 8
email.Contains("@")
email != ""
email.Split("@")
q.why: Contains returns True or False. Length is a length check and != "" is a presence check.

q.q: Which construct runs statements one after another in the order written?
o: Selection
Iteration
Nesting
Sequence
q.why: That is the definition of sequence.

q.q: x = 7. IF x > 10 THEN OUTPUT "A" ELSE IF x > 5 THEN OUTPUT "B" ELSE OUTPUT "C". What is output?
o: B
C
A
B and C
q.why: x > 10 is False; x > 5 is True, so B is output and the ELSE is skipped.

q.q: In an ELSE IF chain, how many branches run?
o: Every branch whose condition is True
All of the branches, one after another
Only the first branch whose condition is True, or the ELSE if none is True
None, unless the chain ends with an ELSE
q.why: Once a True condition is found, the rest of the chain is skipped.

q.q: In the kayak program, the rate is 12 if hours <= 2, else 10 if hours <= 5, else 8. What does 5 hours cost?
q.why: 5 <= 5 is True, so the rate is £10: 5 × 10 = £50.

q.q: In the kayak program, the rate is 12 if hours <= 2, else 10 if hours <= 5, else 8. What does 6 hours cost?
q.why: Both tests are False, so the ELSE sets the rate to 8: 6 × 8 = £48.

q.q: What is a nested IF?
o: An IF inside another IF, so the inner condition is only tested when the outer one is True
An IF followed by a chain of ELSE IF statements, each tested in turn
An IF inside a loop, so the condition is tested every time round
Two separate IFs written one after the other, each with its own condition
q.why: A nested IF is reached only when the outer condition is True.

q.q:
IF member = "Y" THEN
 IF age < 18 THEN OUTPUT "Junior member: £3"
 ELSE OUTPUT "Member: £5"
 END IF
ELSE OUTPUT "Visitor: £8"
END IF
What is output when member = "N" and age = 12?
o: Visitor: £8
Junior member: £3
Member: £5
Nothing is output
q.why: The outer condition is False, so the inner IF is never tested and the ELSE outputs Visitor: £8.

q.q: Using the nested IF for club prices, what is output when member = "Y" and age = 18?
o: Junior member: £3
Member: £5
Visitor: £8
Junior member: £3 and Member: £5
q.why: member is Y, and 18 < 18 is False, so the inner ELSE runs.

q.q: To test the kayak pricing (12 if hours <= 2, else 10 if hours <= 5, else 8), which set of test values checks each boundary?
o: 2, 3, 5 and 6 hours
1, 4 and 7 hours
0, 10, 20 and 30 hours
2 and 5 hours only
q.why: Test the values on each side of each boundary, where > and >= give different results.

q.q: How many times does for (int i = 3; i < 7; i++) run its body?
q.why: i takes the values 3, 4, 5 and 6.

q.q: How many times does for (int i = 1; i < 10; i++) run its body?
q.why: i runs from 1 to 9; it stops before 10. This is a common off-by-one slip.

q.q: Which loop always runs its body at least once?
o: WHILE
FOR
REPEAT…UNTIL (do…while in C#)
foreach
q.why: The condition is tested at the end, after the first run.

q.q: Which kind of loop is a do … while loop in C#?
o: Pre-test, may run zero times
Post-test, always runs at least once
Count-controlled, runs a set number of times
Infinite, never stops
q.why: The condition is at the end, so the body runs once before it is first tested.

q.q: x = 10. WHILE x > 0: x = x − 3. After the loop, what is x?
q.why: x goes 10, 7, 4, 1, −2; −2 > 0 is False so the loop stops.

q.q: Which describes a FOR loop?
o: Condition-controlled: it repeats until a condition changes
Post-test: it always runs at least once
Sentinel-controlled: it stops when a special value is typed
Count-controlled (unconditional): it repeats a known number of times
q.why: FOR is count-controlled; WHILE and REPEAT are condition-controlled.

q.q: What is a sentinel value?
o: The starting value given to a counter before a loop begins
The largest value a loop counter can reach
A value that causes the program to crash
A special input, such as −1, that tells the loop the data has finished
q.why: A sentinel signals the end of the data.

q.q: A WHILE loop reads scores until −1 is typed, adding each to total and adding 1 to count. The inputs are 5, 8, 3 and −1. What is output by Console.WriteLine(count + " scores, total " + total);?
o: 4 scores, total 15
4 scores, total 16
3 scores, total 16
3 scores, total 15
q.why: −1 stops the loop and is not added: 5 + 8 + 3 = 16 from 3 scores.

q.q: x = 10; while (x != 0) { x = x - 3; } Why is this an infinite loop?
o: x is never changed inside the loop
x goes 10, 7, 4, 1, −2 and so on, never equalling 0
The condition is tested at the end, so it runs once more than needed
x reaches 0 after four passes, but the loop ignores it
q.why: The test can never be met because x jumps from 1 to −2.

q.q: A program needs to calculate an average from a running total in a loop. Where should the average be calculated?
o: Inside the loop, every time a value is added
Before the loop, so it is ready to be updated
In the loop condition, so it is checked each time
After the loop, using the final total
q.why: Initialise before, update inside, and calculate and output after the loop.

q.q: What is a subroutine?
o: A named, self-contained block of code that carries out one task and can be called many times
A loop that repeats a block of code a known number of times
A variable declared inside a block of code that only exists while it runs
A built-in method provided by the language, such as Console.WriteLine
q.why: A subroutine is written once and called by name. In C# subroutines are methods.

q.q: A subroutine carries out a task and sends back one value. What is it?
o: A function
A procedure
A parameter
A constant
q.why: Functions return a value; procedures do not.

q.q: Which C# keyword marks a subroutine that returns nothing?
o: static
return
null
void
q.why: A void method is a procedure.

q.q: In static int Total(int a, int b), what are a and b?
o: Arguments
Parameters
Return values
Local constants
q.why: They are listed in the definition to receive the values passed in. The actual values passed in the call are arguments.

q.q: What is a local variable?
o: A variable declared at the top of the program that every subroutine can use
A variable declared inside a subroutine that exists only while it runs and cannot be seen elsewhere
A variable that holds the value returned by a function
A variable whose value cannot change while the program runs
q.why: Local variables exist only inside the subroutine.

q.q: Which is a benefit of user-defined functions?
o: The code always runs faster than without functions
Each function can be tested separately before it is combined with others
No testing is needed once a function has been written
Programs no longer need variables
q.why: Independent (unit) testing is a key benefit, along with reuse, maintenance, readability and teamwork.

q.q: What is the difference between a user-defined function and a built-in function such as Math.Sqrt?
o: A user-defined function returns a value; a built-in function never does
A user-defined function is written by the programmer; a built-in function is provided by the language
A built-in function is written by the programmer; a user-defined function is provided by the language
A user-defined function cannot have parameters; a built-in function can
q.why: Built-in functions such as Convert.ToInt32 and Math.Round are called but not written by you.

q.q: Why do programs store data in files?
o: So the program code can be translated into machine code
So the data is kept after the program ends, because RAM is volatile
So the program does not need to use any variables
So that loops in the program run faster
q.why: Files on secondary storage give persistent storage.

q.q: What are the three steps of file handling, in order?
o: Read, open, write
Open, read or write, close
Create, write, delete
Open, close, read or write
q.why: Always close the file; unclosed files may not save all their data and can stay locked.

q.q: Which C# statement opens results.txt so new data is added to the end?
o: new StreamWriter("results.txt")
new StreamWriter("results.txt", true)
new StreamReader("results.txt")
new StreamReader("results.txt", true)
q.why: The true argument selects append mode. Without it, StreamWriter overwrites the file.

q.q: A program opens scores.txt with new StreamWriter("scores.txt") and writes one line. What happens to the data already in the file?
o: It is overwritten, so only the new line remains
It is kept, and the new line is added to the end
It is kept, and the new line is added to the start
The program crashes because the file already exists
q.why: Write mode creates a new file or overwrites an existing one.

q.q: What does sr.ReadLine() return when there are no more lines in the file?
o: null
q.why: null signals the end of the file and ends the WHILE loop.

q.q: What happens if a program tries to open a missing file for reading?
o: A new empty file is created automatically and read
The compiler refuses to translate the program
The program reads the data from the last file that was opened
An execution (run-time) error occurs that crashes the program, unless it is checked or trapped
q.why: Check File.Exists first or trap the error with try … catch.

q.q: In a FileStream, what does FileMode.CreateNew do?
o: Creates a new file, overwriting any existing file with that name
Creates a new file, but gives an error if the file already exists
Opens an existing file and adds data to the end
Opens an existing file, but gives an error if it is missing
q.why: CreateNew errors if the file exists; Create overwrites it.

q.q: Each line of a scores file is "Name,Score". What is each line called, and how is it separated into fields when read?
o: A field; its records are separated using Split(',')
A record; its fields are separated using Substring
An array; its elements are separated using IndexOf(',')
A record; its fields are separated using Split(',')
q.why: Each line is one record, and Split(',') separates its fields.
